subject: Soft-commit grace period and burst surcharge — term clarifications
messages:
From: Sam Cho <sam.cho@aurum.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@aurum.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on soft-commit grace period & burst surcharge (term sheet v3 attached)

Hi Monica / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked great for our triage workflows. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of pricing clarifications before we send this to legal:

1) Soft-commit / grace period: The term sheet mentions a 30-day soft-commit window and a minimum monthly spend. Can you confirm whether credits for under-delivery in that window roll forward or reduce the minimum on a pro-rata basis?

2) On-demand overage vs commit: When we burst above the committed tokens, is the overage priced as a flat per-token rate (on-demand) or is there a separate burst surcharge % on top of on-demand? We need the exact math because our finance team will model worst-case.

3) True-up cadence: Are true-ups monthly or quarterly? If monthly, is there any lookback smoothing to avoid penalizing a single month spike?

4) Example: our attached usage_samples.csv shows a one-time spike to ~5x baseline in month 3. Show us an example invoice line for that month under both options (flat on-demand overage vs on-demand + 25% "burst surcharge").

I attached the term sheet v3 and a small sample usage export. If easier, happy to hop on a 30-min call next week.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Cho
Head of Platform Integrations
Aurum Health

Attachments:
- Aurum_Redwood_TermSheet_v3.pdf (application/pdf)
- usage_samples.csv (text/csv)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@aurum.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 12:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on soft-commit grace period & burst surcharge (term sheet v3 attached)

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear asks and the sample. Quick answers below and an explicit worked example at the end.

Summary answers:
- Soft-commit (30d): unused commit in the soft window does NOT expire immediately; we roll it forward for a single following billing period as a credit. After that it converts to a standard minimum spend shortfall and is settled in the true-up.
- Overage pricing: there are two configurable behaviors we offer (either can be applied per deal):
   a) Flat on-demand: overage billed at our standard on-demand per-token rate (no surcharge).
   b) Burst-surcharge: on-demand rate + a percentage surcharge (we typically use 20–30% for uncontrolled bursts).
- True-up cadence: monthly by default. Option for quarterly true-up with 30d smoothing window to average out spikes.

What that means for Aurum (proposed deal-specific options):
- Option A (conservative): 3M token monthly commit, 10% volume discount to hosted-per-token rate, flat on-demand overage at $0.00022/token, monthly true-up. No burst surcharge.
- Option B (protective for us): 3M token commit, 12% discount, on-demand at $0.00020/token + 25% burst surcharge applied if monthly usage > 200% of commit. Quarterly true-up with smoothing.

Worked example (month 3 spike in your CSV):
- Commit: 3,000,000 tokens
- Baseline on-demand rate pre-discount: $0.00025/token
- Option A pricing: committed tokens billed at discounted rate ($0.000225 if 10% discount). Additional tokens beyond 3M billed at $0.00022/token.
   * Usage = 15,000,000 tokens (5x spike) -> Overage = 12,000,000 tokens -> Overage charge = 12,000,000 * $0.00022 = $2,640.
- Option B pricing: committed tokens billed at $0.00022 (12% off), on-demand = $0.00020, burst surcharge 25% applies because usage >200% -> effective on-demand = $0.00025.
   * Overage charge = 12,000,000 * $0.00025 = $3,000.

Next steps:
- Tell me which option Aurum prefers (A or B) and whether you want monthly or quarterly true-ups.
- If you want a hybrid (monthly true-ups + a 2-month grace smoothing), we can draft that but will likely sit between A and B on effective price.

If you prefer, I can push a redline to the attached term sheet with Option A and Option B sections for easy comparison. Available for a 30-min call Mon/Tue next week.

Best,
Monica Patel
Sr. Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Monica — I think Option B is reasonable from a risk perspective for us.

Quick internal note you can share if helpful: we can offer up to a 12% discount at the 3M commit level if we include a 25% burst surcharge that only triggers when monthly usage > 200% of commit. Legal will want the exact trigger language and the smoothing/true-up cadence spelled out.

I added a proposed sentence below you can paste into the term sheet: 
"In the event that a Customer's usage in a calendar month exceeds 200% of the committed monthly tokens, all tokens consumed beyond the committed amount for that month shall be billed at the on-demand per-token rate plus a burst surcharge of 25%."

Monica / Ben — thanks for the clear breakdown. Aurum preference and counterpoints below: 

- Preference: Option A from a cash-flow perspective (flat on-demand overage). Procurement is worried about unpredictability from a surcharge.
- Counterproposal: We will accept Option A if Redwood agrees to either: (a) cap the single-month burst surcharge exposure to $40k (i.e., convert any bucket above that to a staged true-up over next 2 months), or (b) include a 60-day lookback smoothing for the first 6 months of the contract. Either mechanism helps our CFO model worst-case.
- True-up: monthly is fine if we add a single 30-day smoothing for months with >300% spikes.

If you can push a redline implementing one of the two protections above, we can move to legal review immediately. Also, we'd like the term sheet to explicitly state the invoice line example (numbers above) so legal doesn't have to ask later.

Available to take that redline review Tue/Wed afternoon.

Best,
Sam
Sam Cho
Head of Platform Integrations
Aurum Health
